title: Check the packaged app
summary: A packaged desktop app can behave differently from the development folder.
introduction: A packaged desktop app can behave differently from the development folder. Your task: List two file paths to check in a packaged build.

blocks.text: A packaged desktop app can behave differently from the development folder. Test its files, permissions and error paths after packaging.

Use a local Electron project with electron installed as a dev dependency and main.cjs as its main file. Run with npx electron . after creating package.json and index.html. These APIs do not run in a web-page playground.

blocks.code:
Use a maintained Electron packaging tool such as Electron Forge.
Build for a supported target platform.
Open the packaged app.
Check local images and scripts.
Test bridge success and failure.
Confirm no renderer Node access or unexpected new windows.
blocks.title: Check the packaged app

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: A packaged build must include every local resource its HTML requests.
Testing the bridge failure path checks that denied or failed desktop operations still produce a useful message.

blocks.text: The check finds missing bundled files and unsafe assumptions before sharing the app.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Packaging is not the same as code signing or automatic updates. Configure those separately when you plan real distribution.
